Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval ([[def-interval]]), and let $\chi:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then the pair $$(\varphi,A):=T_\chi(0,0)=(-\partial_t\chi,\ 
abla\chi)$$ is a potential pair of class $C^1$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ whose field pair is the zero field pair: $$E(\varphi,A)=-
abla(-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(
abla\chi)=0,\qquad B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I$$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the first identity by the equality of the mixed partials $
abla\partial_t\chi=\partial_t
abla\chi$ of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the second by [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]. Explicit instance: for $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $ eta\in\mathbb R$ and $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x- eta t$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, the pair is the constant pair $(\varphi,A)=( eta,a)$, with $E=-
abla eta-\partial_t a=0$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}a=0$ by [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. This pair is nonzero if and only if $( eta,a)
e(0,0)$; for $ eta=0$ and $a=0$ it is exactly the zero pair. To exhibit noninjectivity explicitly, take $ eta=0$ and $a=e_1=(1,0,0)$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$. Then $(\varphi,A)=(0,e_1)$ and $(0,0)$ are distinct potential pairs with the same zero field pair. Thus the map from potential pairs to field pairs of [[def-em-fields]] is not injective: nonzero potentials may represent the zero field pair (pure-gauge fields), and no nonzero value of $\varphi$ or $A$ alone is evidence for a nonzero field, consistently with [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] and [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. The example is a statement about the representation of the zero field configuration; it asserts no Maxwell equation, no source configuration and no empirical situation.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: Apply the gauge transformation $T_\chi$ to the zero pair $(0,0)$, using the linearity of the componentwise partial derivatives and of the gradient ([[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). The field pair of the zero pair is $(0,0)$; by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] the transformed pair has the same field pair, which is $(0,0)$. The explicit formulas are then recomputed directly: with $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x-\beta t$ one has $\partial_t\chi=-\beta$ and $\nabla\chi=a$, so $(\varphi,A)=(\beta,a)$; the fields of a constant pair vanish because every partial derivative of a constant is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Both computations use only the definitions; no choice principle and no hypothesis on $\Omega$ or $I$ beyond openness and being an interval are used. The formula $(\varphi,A)=(\beta,a)$ includes all zero and nonzero parameter choices. Equality of this constant pair to zero is equivalent, component by component, to $\beta=0$ and $a=0$. Noninjectivity is established by the particular nonzero witness $a=e_1$, $\beta=0$, compared with the zero pair; it is not inferred by claiming that every parameter choice is nonzero.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $ho:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega	imes I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,ho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG= rac{ho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+
abla G=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega	imes I$. (c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose additionally that the given potential pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega	imes I$. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations
$$W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$
The source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are automatic for a potential pair. For an arbitrary given $C^2$ potential pair, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge and these wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative. In full generality their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations in (a), including $-\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$. Thus the equivalence with decoupled waves holds within the declared Lorenz gauge, without asserting gauge reachability. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (b) Direct expansion of $T_\chi$: $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=\operatorname{div}A+\Delta\chi+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi-c^{-2}\partial_t^2\chi=G-W\chi$, using linearity and the $C^2$ mixed-partials identity for $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the field part is [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. (c) Under the explicitly imposed hypothesis $G=0$, the continuously defined derivatives $\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$ vanish. Substitution in (a) turns the two sourced residual equations exactly into $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$. Conversely those two wave equations with $G=0$ make the residual equations hold, and the two source-free equations were already proved for every potential pair. There is no inference from Maxwell alone to a gauge condition; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. All statements are pointwise on $\Omega	imes I$; the constants $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ are those of the framework postulates ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]). No choice principle, no hypothesis on the shape of $\Omega$ and no solvability of $W\chi=G$ is used.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Let $c>0$, let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega:=c|k|$, and let $$\chi(x,t):=\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t),$$ the real part of the complex plane wave $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with wave vector $k$ and frequency $\omega=c|k|$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then $\chi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $W\chi=0$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ ([[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); indeed $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\chi$, $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\chi$ and $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$, so $W\chi=c^{-2}(-c^2|k|^2\chi)+|k|^2\chi=0$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Consequently, for every potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^2$ jointly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the gauge-transformed pair satisfies $$G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)\qquad\text{and}\qquad E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\quad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)$$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]); in particular, if $(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair. Explicitly $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$ and $\nabla\chi=-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, so $\varphi'=\varphi-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, $A'=A-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$; the zero pair is in Lorenz gauge and its transform $(-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t),\ -k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t))$ is a nonzero pair that remains in Lorenz gauge and still represents the zero field pair. Thus the Lorenz condition does not determine the potential pair. The example is the residual generator $W\chi=0$ of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] on the free-space branch; on a bounded domain with prescribed gauge boundary data the admissible generators are restricted, and no such data-dependent claim is made here.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: Compute with the chain and product rules: $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\cos\theta$, $\nabla\chi=-k\sin\theta$ and $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\cos\theta$ at $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substitute $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$ to get $W\chi=0$. Then use the gauge-shift identity and field invariance of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b) and [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]; the class bookkeeping is that of [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. No choice principle is used and no boundary condition is imposed, matching the free-space branch of the gauge-reachability statement on this page.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$. Fix a smooth time-independent Dirichlet datum $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$. Then there is a gauge function $\psi$, of class $C^\infty$ on a neighbourhood of $\bar\Omega\times\bar I$, with $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ for every $t\in I$, such that $$\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\text{ for every }t\in I;$$ the transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge on $\Omega\times I$ and has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). The generator is unique among such generators with datum $g$; if $g=0$, then $\psi$ is the unique generator with zero boundary values. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is the fixed time-independent Dirichlet datum $g$ and the Neumann variant with its own compatibility condition for every $t$ is not claimed; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy:
(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) Fix $g$ and let $h\in C^\infty( ar\Omega)$ be the solution of $-\varepsilon_0\Delta h=0$ in $\Omega$ with $h|_{\partial\Omega}=g$ ([[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$ and $ho=0$). Let $R$ be the zero-trace Dirichlet solution operator of $-\Delta$: for $F\in L^2(\Omega)$, $R(F)\in H_0^1\cap H^2$ is the unique weak solution of $-\Delta R(F)=F/\varepsilon_0$, equivalently $-\varepsilon_0\Delta R(F)=F$. Existence and uniqueness are [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with datum $0$ and source $ho=F$; the $L^2$ bound $\|R(F)\|_{L^2}\le(2L)^2\varepsilon_0^{-1}\|F\|_{L^2}$ follows by testing with $R(F)$ and using the squared Poincare bound of [[lem-em-zero-boundary-coercivity]] (constant $(2L)^2$, nonsquared consequence $\|v\|_2\le2L\|
abla v\|_2$), and $R$ maps $H^k(\Omega)$ boundedly into $H^{k+2}(\Omega)$ with constant $C_k$ depending only on $k,\Omega$ by [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]] applied to $L=-\Delta$ on the bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $F_t:=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\in C^\infty( ar\Omega)$ and $\psi(\cdot,t):=h+R(F_t)$. Then $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi(\cdot,t)=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)$, so $\operatorname{div}(A+
abla\psi)(\cdot,t)=0$, and $\psi(\cdot,t)|_{\partial\Omega}=g$, for every $t$. Joint smoothness: by linearity of $R$ the difference quotient of $\psi$ in $t$ is $R$ of the difference quotient of $F_t$; since $t\mapsto F_t$ is $C^\infty$ as a map into each $H^k$ (all mixed derivatives of $A$ are jointly continuous and $ ar\Omega	imes ar I$ is compact) and $R$ is bounded $H^k	o H^{k+2}$ and $L^2	o L^2$, induction gives $\partial_t^j\psi(\cdot,t)=R(\partial_t^jF_t)$ for every $j$, a continuous map into every $H^m$, hence into every Sobolev space whose embedding into $C^\ell( ar\Omega)$ is supplied by [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] (the bounded $C^\infty$ domain is a bounded extension domain); every mixed derivative $\partial_x^\alpha\partial_t^j\psi=\partial_x^\alpha R(\partial_t^jF_t)$ is therefore jointly continuous on $ ar\Omega	imes ar I$, so $\psi$ is $C^\infty$ in the extension sense and its transform is defined. The field pair is unchanged by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] and the condition $\operatorname{div}(A+
abla\psi)=0$ is Coulomb gauge in the chosen chart. Uniqueness: two generators with the same datum $g$ have a difference that is harmonic on $\Omega$ with zero Dirichlet trace, hence zero, by the uniqueness clause of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](a) with $ho=0$. (c) Put $\delta\varphi:=	ilde\varphi-\varphi$, $\delta A:=	ilde A-A$. Then $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=0$ and $-
abla\delta\varphi-\partial_t\delta A=0$; since $\delta A$ is jointly $C^2$ with $\operatorname{curl}\delta A(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, the scalar clause of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]] gives $\chi_0\in C^2$ jointly with $\delta A=
abla\chi_0$. Then $
abla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t
abla\chi_0=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$ (mixed partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi_0$, [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), and $\Omega$ is star-shaped hence connected, so $\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0=h(t)$ for a $C^1$ function $h$ of $t$ alone. Choose $\eta\in C^2(I)$ with $\eta'=-h$ and set $\chi:=\chi_0+\eta$; then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi_0+h,\ A+
abla\chi_0)=(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)$. Finally $G(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi$ by [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b), and both $G$-values vanish, so $W\chi=0$. The linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ used throughout is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; $H^m$ notation is [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and the elliptic problems use the domains of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. The declared Choice assumptions enter only through the elliptic existence theorem and the wave supplier and are carried in the statement. No claim beyond (a)-(c) is made.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.disposition: unchanged actual use of wave-form(b), reviewed; independent radial/regularity lane remains held

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the upper face $z=b$ has outward flux $L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and the lower face $z=a$ has outward flux $-L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$. Their respective signed contributions to the field-energy change are $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0cE_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.

B_example_thought_consumer_note: Energy-flow and pure-gauge examples remain leaves; no actual consumers. Wave form direct consumers use unchanged gauge transformation/residual identity(b), so its corrected(c) equivalence introduces no additional current consumer rewrite.
